title: Start-up: the window is shown at about 40 ms and does not answer for about 0.8 s

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens (CamCraft 0.25.0, Windows 11, release build, Intel integrated GPU, DX12)
Another process polled the window every 2 ms.
- The window is visible at about 40 ms (864x522) and resized at about 100 to 190 ms.
- It does not answer messages until about 730 to 1080 ms (3 runs, 5 MB project).
- Any SetWindowPos or ShowWindow call from another process blocks until then.
- With no project on the command line the freeze is the same length.

## Where the time goes
I added temporary timing lines (not in the patch). Milliseconds from `run_windowed`, release build:

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Window created | 22 |
| GPU bring-up done | 226 |
| `StockEye::new` done | 658 |
| First frame start | 669 |
| Project loaded (5 MB) | 683 (14 ms) |
| First frame presented | 727 |

So the project load is not the cause. `StockEye::new` is about 430 ms. It compiles the composite and trace shaders. It runs on the UI thread before the first frame, but the eye is only used for the traced stock view. The browser shell already builds it after the first frame (`StockEye::new_async`).

## Patch (ready on a branch)
Build the eye on a worker thread (`shell_window/eye_boot.rs`). The shell takes it on a later frame. Until then the viewport draws the stock sheet. The eye syncs its sample count on its first frame (`apply_quality`).

Same probe, 3 runs each: first responsive at 730, 806 and 1079 ms before; 344, 369 and 448 ms after.

## Not fixed
About 300 ms remain: GPU bring-up (about 200 ms) and the first frame. Fixing it needs the bring-up off the UI thread, or the window created hidden and shown after the first frame. That is a larger design change. Which does the maintainer prefer?

Tests: unit tests for the hand-off (`eye_boot`). `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` passes (1479 tests) when it runs to the end. Not run: the gate tiers, clippy (not installed here), other platforms.

Separate note: on plain `main` (without this patch) the same test binary sometimes ends with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` at a random point (8 of 15 runs on Windows 11). The patch does not cause this. I can open a separate issue for it if wanted.

title: A script cannot open a project in the CamCraft window without taking the focus

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
A script starts `camcraft-ui some.camproj` from a background process. The window takes the foreground. The script cannot prevent this.

## What happens (CamCraft 0.25.0, Windows 11)
- The launcher sets STARTUPINFO `wShowWindow` to `SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE` (7) or `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` (4). This has no effect.
- The window is visible and not minimized at about 40 ms after launch.
- The window is the foreground window from that time.

I polled with EnumWindows, IsWindowVisible, GetWindowRect and GetForegroundWindow.

## Cause (found in the code)
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_window.rs` (`init_gpu`) creates the window with default attributes. In winit 0.30.13 a visible, active window is shown with `ShowWindow(SW_SHOW)` (`window_state.rs`, `apply_diff`).
- The same function then calls `window.focus_window()`. On Windows this sends a synthetic Alt key press to get past the foreground lock, so the lock timeout does not matter.
- Nothing in the program reads the launcher's show state.

## Proposal
Two new start options in the `cli_options` table:
- `--no-activate`: create the window inactive and do not call `focus_window()`. The window shows, and the focused window keeps the focus.
- `--minimized`: the same, and the window starts minimized. It covers no other window.

The default does not change. A separate step could read STARTUPINFO on Windows. That is a larger change, so it is not proposed here.

A patch is ready on a branch. It has unit tests for the parser and the window attributes. I also checked both options with the project on the command line, from a process started by Task Scheduler (not from a terminal). The window was never the foreground window, and it did not take the focus when the project finished loading. `--minimized` gave a minimized window. Not tested: macOS, Linux.

Is this the wanted shape?

title: Tools: reamer and counterbore tool kinds (split from #897)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Split out of #897 (which also covers spot drill, countersink and center drill, P8): the two hole-making kinds that real tool libraries need most now.

**What happens:** `ToolKind` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs`) has no reamer and no counterbore. Such a tool can only be stored as a `Drill` or `EndMill`, losing what makes it different, or not at all.

**Why now:** converting one user's real tool libraries to `.camtools` (14 libraries, community converter bnegt/Fusitool2Craftool), 2487 reamers and 42 counterbores were skipped because CamCraft has no kind for them - the largest group of unconvertible tools after missing feed/speed data. CamCraft already has the cycle side: reaming (G85) and dwell/boring cycles shipped with #1445.

**What the kinds need (from general machining references - Machinery's Handbook, ISO/DIN reamer and counterbore standards, public tooling catalogs):**
- **Reamer:** diameter, flute length, number of flutes, lead (chamfer) angle and length, overall/shank; its cutting data runs slower than a drill of the same size (per-material rows, #890); a hole op with a reamer uses the reaming cycle and expects a pre-drilled hole (finish allowance).
- **Counterbore:** cutting diameter, pilot diameter (or none) and pilot length, flat bottom, flute length; a hole op cuts to a stated depth with a dwell at the bottom.
- Both: spun outline that the simulation and the reach/gouge checks read (safety floor: effort high), `.camtools` file version bump with old files still loading, MCP `add_tool` / `edit_tool` kinds, catalog entries.

**Clean-room:** specify geometry and behaviour from the public references above. Do not use Fusion's tool-library schema or the converter's Fusion-side code (also GPL-3.0) as a spec - the converter only showed how many tools are missing.

**Done means:** a reamer and a counterbore can be created, saved and reloaded in `.camtools`; a reaming op and a counterbore op generate, simulate and verify clean on a plate fixture with the tool's real outline; old `.camtools` files load unchanged; pinned by tests.

title: Project save writes the `.camproj` file in place: a failed write destroys the old project

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happened**

`project::save` writes the new project text directly into the target `.camproj` file (`crates/app/src/project/wire.rs:296-304` on `main` f14097855):

```rust
if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(path, &text) {
```

`std::fs::write` truncates the file first and then writes the new bytes. If the write stops before the end, the old project is gone and the new project is incomplete. This can occur when:

- the disk or the USB stick becomes full;
- the connection to a network share stops;
- the app or the computer stops during the write.

A cloud-sync client (OneDrive, Dropbox) or a backup tool can also read the file while it is half written, and copy the incomplete file to other computers.

All save routes use this function:

- the window: `State::save_project_path` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4716`);
- the MCP tool `save_project` and the script call `cam.save`: both go through `api::v_save` to `crate::project::save` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:49`).

I found this while I examined how CamCraft projects behave in shared and synced folders.

**Expected**

A failed save keeps the old `.camproj` file as it was. Other programs never see a half-written project file.

CamCraft already does this for machine files and for the fixture library. `machine::store::write_atomic` (`crates/app/src/machine/store.rs:104`) writes a temporary file in the same folder, flushes it, and renames it over the target. On a failure, it removes the temporary file, and the target stays as it was. `fixture_library/store.rs` has its own copy of the same steps (line 107).

**Steps to reproduce**

I found this by code inspection. I did not make a damaged file on a machine.

1. Open a project and save it to a `.camproj` file.
2. Read `project::save` in `crates/app/src/project/wire.rs`: the save opens the existing file with truncation before it writes the new text.
3. Any failure after step 2 leaves a short or empty file in the place of the old project.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at f14097855 (2026-11-22). The same code is in v0.24.0 and v0.25.0. Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- `project::save` calls `machine::store::write_atomic`. Preferences, recent files, view settings and machine files already use this helper. No new module and no new copy.
- Two refusals of today stay:
  - a save into a folder that does not exist (the helper creates missing folders, so `project::save` checks first);
  - a save over a read-only `.camproj` file. On Linux and macOS, a rename replaces a read-only file, so `project::save` checks first.
- The file format and the saved text do not change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.
- The browser build does not change. It gives the text to a download (`save_text`), not to a file path.
- On Windows, a rename can fail when another program holds the target file open. The save then reports the error, and the old file stays.

**Done means:** `project::save` replaces the target only through a rename of a complete, flushed temporary file in the same folder. A test shows that a failed save keeps the old `.camproj` byte for byte. A test shows that a good save leaves no temporary file. Tests show that a save into a missing folder and a save over a read-only file are refused, and that the old file stays. The `project_roundtrip` tests still pass.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

## What the code does
A program has two operations in one setup: first a five-axis operation that leans the tool (5-Axis Contour, Flow, Swarf), then a 3-axis operation with the tool upright.

1. The tilted section ends with the tool still tilted. Its exit rapids keep the pose (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs`, near line 210).
2. `dump()` in `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` keeps the state `tilted` for one operation only (lines 430 and 520-541). The first upright move of the next operation gets no angles.
3. `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`: `endPreamble` (786-838) resets `tcpmOn` and `lastA/B/C` in the script only. `startPreamble` (742) writes `G49` only. No block writes `A0` or `B0`. `retractHome` is `G28 Z0` with no rotary axis.
4. `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `endPreamble` (873-905) resets `lastA/B/C` only. `startPreamble` writes `G49` only.

Result, by reading: the posted program has no rotary word between the last tilted move and the first cut of the upright operation. The machine stays at the last tilted angles, and the 3-axis operation cuts with the tool or the table tilted. That is wrong posted G-code (a gouge or a collision), and no check stops it:

- `first_traverse_posed` judges only the first operation of the post order (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3325`).
- No check compares the pose at the end of one operation with the start of the next.

## Posts that are safe, by the same read
- `tormach.cps` writes `G53 G0 Z` and `G0 A0` at the first upright move of a section (718-775).
- `mach4.cps` writes `G00 A<zero> C<zero>` when the stored lean is different (about 575-625).
- The posts that refuse a tilted move cannot post the first operation.

1. A test that posts a tilted operation followed by an upright operation with `fanuc.cps` on `tilthead.mch` and with `doosan-dnm.cps`. It shows the blocks between the two sections. If the program states the angles, close this issue with that evidence.
2. If it does not: each section that follows a tilted section states the rotary position before its first approach, at a safe height (the pattern of PR #3421 for the opening of a tilted section, and of `tormach.cps`). The same for a tool change between the two, and for the same tool in the two operations.
3. A check in the app: an upright operation after a tilted one posts only when the return to upright is stated, else a refusal with a diagnostic.
4. The same test for each post that supports a rotary axis.

G0 X34
G0 Z-71.5
G1 X30 Z-71.5 F0.025

The part-off blade's +Z flank stands at or behind the part's end plane (posted -Z corner at Z -73.0 for this 3 mm blade), or the operation is refused; a part-off that cuts into the part is a gouge and holds the post.

title: Fanuc inch post can write a full-circle G03 for a short arc

labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The native `post` command accepts two short counterclockwise arcs and writes two G03 blocks with coincident start and end XY coordinates. Both blocks have a nonzero center offset. A control that treats these blocks as full circles can cut a circle instead of a short stroke.

I reproduced this with CamCraft `post 0.25.0 (boa_engine)` and the original `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`. The post, CL reader and post script match main at `b44a422bb`. I checked the generated file. No controller or machine ran it.

## Reproduce

Save the following synthetic input as `tiny.cnc`. The coordinates in the intermediate file use micrometres.

```
; HSMW-CNC v1
PARAM OperationName Arc precision witness
PARAM SpindleSpeed 6000
PARAM WorkOffset 1
PARAM OriginX 0
PARAM OriginY 0
PARAM OriginZ 0
PARAM ToolDiameter 4
PARAM ClearancePlane 18
PARAM RetractPlane 18
PARAM TopOfStock 6
TOOL 1 EM-0400-2FL
SECTION Arc precision witness
Rapid X 18123 Y 5432 Z 18000
Plunge X 18123 Y 5432 Z 5500 F 45000
Arc CCW X 18123 Y 5433 Z 5500 F 180000 I 10123 J 5432
Arc CCW X 18123 Y 5434 Z 5500 F 180000 I 10123 J 5432
Rapid X 18123 Y 5434 Z 18000
ENDSECTION
```

Run `cargo run -p camcraft-post --bin post -- --units inch assets/posts/fanuc.cps tiny.cnc tiny.nc`.

The input Y positions are 5432, 5433 and 5434 µm. Each arc has a sweep of about 0.00716°. In the NC file, the preceding position and both arc endpoints are X0.7135 Y0.2139. Each arc reads:

```text
G03 X0.7135 Y0.2139 Z0.2165 I-0.315 J0. F7.09
```

The command exited successfully. It reported 13 mapped records, nine blocks and zero swallowed records.

## Expected

The post must preserve the short motion at the selected precision or refuse it with a diagnostic. It must distinguish a short arc from an intended full turn. Pin this input through the native post command. Also check a representable short arc and a genuine full circle.

Found while testing #1869. A check in the new sketch generator protects that feature. The native post also accepts intermediate files from other sources. #2191 concerned the radius-word mode and a different rounding failure.

Suggested labels are `bug`, `P1`, `area:post`, `effort:high`, and `source:agent`.

body:
Found by QA brief q08 (AI chat panel with a local model) on v0.25.0 (7e2a8119), Linux x86_64, preset "Offline local (Ollama)", model qwen3-coder:latest.

**What happens:** in a fresh chat on a document with two operations, the request "Delete every operation." made the model call `delete_operation` twice ("Pocket roughing", "Pocket finishing"). Both calls ran at once - cards "Succeeded", no "Confirmation required" banner, no Allow/Deny. The document lost every operation. One Undo (ribbon) brought both back, so nothing was lost for good.

**Why:** `requires_confirmation` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/transport.rs` only asks in Native mode for `open_project` and for the live gate's kinds (`requires_approval` in `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs`: post, file paths and writes, machine and limit edits). Destructive document edits (`delete_operation`, `delete_tool`, `delete_setup`, `delete_model`, ...) are never confirmed. The q08 brief and issue 3411 ("delete every operation (confirmation gate holds)") both expect a confirmation or a refusal here.

**Expected:** a delete (at least of operations, tools, setups or models) asked for by the model stops at the inline Allow/Deny banner, like `post` does; Deny sends "User denied tool ..." back to the model and changes nothing. One banner per turn for several deletes is fine.

**Evidence** (fork branch `qa-artifacts`, run q08-20261122T131017Z):
- panel after the turn: https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/28-step6b.png
- get_job before / after / after one Undo: https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/job-06a-restart-baseline.json, https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/job-06b-after-step6-fresh.json, https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/job-06c-after-undo.json
- transcript (raw requests and replies; step 6 is the last turn, session 2): https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/q08-transcript.json
- project to reproduce: https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/q08/q08-20261122T131017Z/q08-after-step5.camproj

**Repro:** `camcraft-ui q08-after-step5.camproj`, Panels > AI Chat, provider "Offline local (Ollama)", model `qwen3-coder:latest`, prompt "Delete every operation." (any model that calls `delete_operation` will do; a scripted transport in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/ai_chat/` reproduces it without a model).

Done means: in Native mode a `delete_operation` (and the other delete tools) from the AI chat waits for Allow/Deny; Deny leaves get_job unchanged and the denial reaches the model; a test in the ai_chat suite pins it (scripted turn with two deletes, Deny, document unchanged).

- The type `machining2d::PassStart { Auto, Inside, Outside }` and its ring law `PassStart::rank` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs`).
- One project key `pass_start` (`project::PassStartDto`). `auto` is never written.
- The generic MCP door `edit_operation`, and one Passes-tab row `Pass starts at` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pass_start_row.rs`).

- Give Bore the field `pass_start` with the same type, key, row and MCP door. Do not make a new type.
- Make the planner of Bore read it. Where to look: the bore planner (the Bore kind in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`).
- Auto must keep the current output of Bore byte for byte (each golden).
- If Bore has no pass order, its row says so by name, and the issue records why.
- Leave room for the start point and the exit point of #1448 beside the parameter.

## Safety

The change can change posted moves. It is under the safety floor. The pin goes red first. The review is an independent read with a hand trace of one level.

Done means: Bore has the option in the property panel, in MCP and in the project file; Inside and Outside force the order; Auto keeps all shipped goldens byte-identical; a pin test shows the forced order.

body:
The "Do not touch" group of the Geometry tab (Boundaries) does not work on a Engrave operation. The group shows only the note "'Do not touch' is supported on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket operations only so far". There is no "Pick protected" button. The maintainer asked for "do not touch" on operations, in his words: "the calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs" (#2055).

Found during the work on #3335. Refs #2055. Refs #3335.

## What to do

1. Add `OpType::Engrave` to `do_not_touch_applies` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`).
2. Make the Engrave generator keep the full tool (flutes, shank and holder) clear of each protected face and edge, by the clearance. This includes the cutting moves, the lead moves, the link moves and the plunges.
3. If the generator cannot keep clear, refuse the operation or mark it "incomplete". The diagnostic names the item. The post is blocked.
4. The verify check and the post gate already check the protected items. Make sure that they read the Engrave moves.

## Safety

This work is under the safety floor: it changes the toolpath and the posted G-code of a Engrave operation that has protected items. A Engrave operation without protected items must give the same toolpath as before. Pin that.

## Done means

- The Boundary group of a Engrave operation shows "Pick protected", and a viewport click adds a face or an edge row.
- A test with a protected face next to the cut shows that no move comes nearer than the clearance.
- A test with a protected face that the cut cannot avoid shows the refusal with the item named, and a blocked post.
- A test shows that a Engrave operation without protected items gives the same toolpath.

title: Performance: the stock simulation is very slow - it runs on the CPU, the GPU shader path is not built

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; performance; P2; the stock simulation; is extremly slow. This was supposed to be calculated on the GPU as a shader, it doesnt seem to be the case..

## What the repository shows

The maintainer is right: the stock removal does not run on the GPU. The plan exists. It is built only in part.

- #2607 (research, closed) decided: "The GPU does the display playback cut. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict. The home for GPU compute code is `camcraft-gpu` (#2620)." It made the slices S1 to S6.
- S1 #2626 (the CPU f32 twin of the cell cut kernel) is merged. It is a CPU twin, by design. It runs no shader.
- #2620 (the `camcraft-gpu` compute crate: probe, cached device, CPU fallback) is NOT merged. Its work is held on the pushed branch `issue/2620-gpu-compute-seam` at `90c98be93`, since 2026-11-19 (the gate stopped for disk space). Its label is `claimed`, P4.
- S2 #2627 (the WGSL removal kernel for ball and flat tools, linear moves), S3 #2629 (viewport playback on the GPU, with CPU fallback), S4 #2628, S5 #2630 and S6 #2631 are open at P4. S3 to S6 are `blocked`.
- So the playback in the viewport still uses the CPU engines. A long program is slow.

## What the maintainer needs

The Simulate view plays a program at a usable speed, with a visible stock cut. The frame target is under 10 ms for a still frame (`docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`).

## Plan

1. Measure first. A scout and a worker time the playback on a real program (the `fig8` 2D Offset, EM-0800-4FL, and one 3D Pocket). The numbers go in a comment: cells, moves, milliseconds for each frame and for the cut. This shows where the time goes: the cut, the mesh, the upload, or the frame.
2. Quick wins on the CPU path that the measure shows, if any. Each has a counter test (AGENTS.md "Frame cost").
3. Finish the GPU path in order: #2620, then #2627 (S2), then #2629 (S3). Raise their priority to P2 and the type to bug (they are the fix of this issue). S4, S5 and S6 stay P4 and follow.
4. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict (the verify check, the collision check, the post gate). The GPU result is display only. A machine without a usable GPU falls back to the CPU path and says so.

## Safety

The simulation that blocks the post is not changed by this work. Any change to the f64 engines is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- A recorded measure before and after, in a comment.
- On the reference machine, the Simulate view of a `fig8` program plays at a usable frame rate.
- A counter test: a still frame cuts nothing again.
- A CPU fallback test for a machine without a GPU.

> bug; Movement calcualtion; P2; Example 2D offset set with a outside continment, helixes dowwn inside of the calculated "containmen" and works its way from the inside out.. A 2D Offset operation has the containment "Outside". The tool helixes down inside the calculated containment. It then cuts the passes from the inside out. The result is fully engaged slotting moves in the stock.

An "Outside" containment starts outside the part and works inward. The tool never makes a fully engaged slot in the stock.

## The change that the maintainer suggests

A new option on the Passes tab: "Pass starts at", with the values Auto, Inside and Outside.
- Auto keeps the current behaviour.
- Inside and Outside force the order.

The user then controls the order and stops the slots. This follows the rule that a strategy fork is an operation parameter with a default.

## Evidence

- Build v0.25.0, commit 7e2a8119 (built 2026-11-22 02:53 UTC). The maintainer sent a screenshot. It is not attached here.
- Operation `2D Offset1`: tool `EM-0800-4FL` (Ø8 end mill), model `fig8`, setup `Setup1`, machine VMC 3-AXIS, post Siemens 840D.

- Lead in / Lead out tab: Entry type Helix, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Level to level "Same as entry", Between levels "Clearance plane", Between passes "Retract plane".
- The simulation at 60.7 / 1392.8 s shows the tool deep inside the machined area. The cut area around it is a closed slot.

#2849, test 3 (`shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`) uses the same model, the same tool and an "Outside" containment. Its body says that the last feed ends 31.406 mm from the part outline, and the PR #3267 says that a ring order change fixes it but turns `corner_arc_radius::the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` red. title: 3D Finish: an option to stop the waterline ring pass on steep flanks

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What is asked

A contributor asks for one control on 3D Finish: a switch that turns off the waterline ring pass, so the operation cuts its raster lines only. The contributor's words, quoted unchanged (chat, 2026-11-19):

> how hard would it be to make a checkbox that can disable the waterline portion?

## What the tool does today

A Parallel 3D Finish operation splits the terrain at 45 degrees. Shallow facets get the Z-following raster lines. Steep facets get waterline rings: `parallel()` runs one raster pass, then `rings_and_tail` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` line 210). The ring paths run about 90 degrees across the raster lines. Every wall that stands above the Bottom plane gets its ring ladder: hole walls, end walls, and the sloped edges of a tilted top face.

The picture below shows a contributor's test part: a long bar with a top face tilted 2 degrees and two openings, cut with a 0.3125 in ball-end, Bottom 0.300 in. The purple arrow marks one ring run that still survives on a wall near the near end. The tall ladders at the far end wall are the same law at the high end of the sloped face. The raster family cannot cover those walls; only the rings can.

![Ring run surviving on a wall at Bottom 0.300 in, parallel to the bar length and near the near end edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2811-waterline-arrow.png)

## Why the switch is wanted

On a part whose steep flanks are out of scope, the rings add cutting time, and they add paths the machinist did not ask for. Some machinists want the lines only, and accept the walls as they stand. One checkbox should say that choice out loud.

## Proposed shape

- One parameter, for example `waterlines: bool`, default on. Existing behaviour does not change.
- GUI name: not just "off". The control must name the consequence, for example "Steep flanks: Waterlines / Leave uncut".
- The switch applies to the Parallel pattern. Whether Parallel multi and Scallop take it is a decision. Blend should likely never take it: its 30-45 degree double cut needs the rings to remove the staircase (its own note says so). The maintainer decides this scope.

## Laws the switch must keep

1. With the switch off and steep flanks present, the path must carry a visible note that names the uncut flanks and their count. Silent rest material is not allowed (Prime Directive).
2. A model that is fully steep with the switch off must refuse with a clear error, not post an empty program. The raster answers `false` for an all-steep model; today "the rings alone carry it".
3. The parameter round-trips in the project file. Old project files load with the default, on.
4. The 3D finish MCP parameter surface exposes the same field (same rule as `fill_openings` and `gap_link`).

## Measured support (headless probe, main `744c0847b`)

Synthetic model: bar 24 x 160 mm, flat bottom z 0, top face sloped 2 degrees, two through openings, ball 7.94 mm, Parallel, gap link Jump. The probe classifies the XY direction of every Feed move.

- Bottom 0: 188 along-wall Y-family Feed runs at Z ladder levels about 0.4 mm apart. Zero Feed runs cross the open top face. All perpendicular feed sits on walls.
- Bottom raised to 9.75 mm (near the high top edge): the same perpendicular runs collapse to three ladder levels per wall, and only over the stretch where the face still stands above Bottom. Nothing sits in the open middle.

This matches the picture: raising Bottom shrank the ring set everywhere except where walls still rise above it. The behaviour is correct as designed; this issue asks for control, not for a defect fix. The probe code can become the pinning test for the switch.

## Done means

- A checkbox flips the ring pass on and off, and each state has a motion test that pins it.
- Off plus steep flanks: a note names the uncut flanks; no ring moves appear in the CL output.
- Off plus a steep-only model: a refusal with a clear message.
- Project-file round-trip test and MCP parity pass.
- The 3D finish page shows the control with its consequence wording.

## Classification

This account is a contributor and cannot set labels. Suggested labels, for a maintainer: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: it changes posted G-code when the switch is used), `area:motion`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The body was written by the contributor's agent at the contributor's request.

## Request

Add a post for Mach3 Mill (3-axis). Mach3 is still on many retrofit mills and routers. The `Mach4` post writes words and macros that Mach3 does not read in the same way.

From the public "Using Mach3Mill" manual (behaviour only):

- No Custom Macro B (`#` variables in expressions). The Mach4 post uses `[...]` expressions in some places; the Mach3 post must write plain numbers only.
- Program end `M30`. Comments `( )`.

- A built-in post `Mach3` and a machine file.

Depends on #2158 and #1861.

## Scope

- Build one global containment forest across all closed contours and open chains on a nested sheet.
- Assign each open chain to its smallest enclosing closed contour, or mark it top-level when outside all parts.

  - Cut internal holes, pockets, and open features of a part before its outer outline.
  - Cut small parts nested inside a hole before the enclosing hole cuts free.
  - Order sibling parts at the same depth by increasing area (small parts before large parts) to preserve router vacuum hold-down and sheet rigidity.
  - Reserve ordered pass phases: marking/scribe passes (`#1447`) first, internal/pocket passes next, rough/onion-skin profile passes next, and final onion-skin breakthrough passes last.
- Compute minimum inside-corner cutter-radius clearance diagnostics when a circular tool (`radius = cut_width / 2`) cannot reach sharp concave corners.
- Validate that no contour cuts after an enclosing contour has already freed its material.

## Done means

Tests in `crates/geometry` verify inside-out cut order across a multi-part sheet containing nested holes, internal open cuts, and a small part placed inside a large hole, verify phase ordering for marking and onion-skin passes, confirm smaller sibling parts precede larger ones deterministically, report concave inside-corner radius limits, and refuse invalid open-chain side requests by name.

This is a research umbrella (`needs-research`). It answers the open questions below in comments. Then it files the concrete sub-issues and closes. No code goes on this issue.

## What exists today

- `camcraft-cli mcp` is an MCP server on stdio. An agent drives one headless document.
- The app can start with `--mcp-port`, and `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` bridges an external agent to the open window. The agent then drives the live document.
- The skill `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/` documents the tools for Claude Code.
- Every MCP tool calls the same undoable commands as the GUI (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool").

## Goal

1. **In-app chat panel.** A dock panel in CamCraft where the user types a request, for example "add a 2D pocket on the selected face with T3". An AI model answers and acts through the same MCP tool set. The panel shows each tool call and its result.
2. **Provider choice.** The user picks the model provider and the model:
   - **Cloud:** Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT/Codex models), Google (Gemini).
   - **Local:** Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp server (most local servers have an OpenAI-compatible API).
3. **External agents.** Each external agent tool gets one documented way to drive the open app (`--mcp-port` plus `mcp --connect`), and a skill or instruction file in its own format:
   - Claude Code: `.claude/skills/` (exists; keep it current);
   - Codex CLI: AGENTS.md section or `.codex/` instructions;
   - Gemini / Antigravity CLI: `GEMINI.md` and `.agents/skills/`;
   - local models through Ollama or Unsloth: a short system prompt plus the tool list.

## Open questions (answer each in a comment)

1. **Panel architecture.** In-process, where the app calls the provider API and maps the MCP tools to the provider's tool-calling format? Or a separate process that speaks MCP to the app? What keeps the UI thread free (async, cancel)?
2. **One tool schema for all providers.** Map the MCP tool schemas to the Anthropic Messages tool format, the OpenAI tools format, and Gemini function declarations. Which local models do tool calling well enough? What is the fallback for a model without tool calling?
3. **Safety.**
   - Every action goes through the undoable commands.
   - The chat never posts G-code, never writes a file, and never changes a machine without a confirmation in the panel.
   - Group one chat turn as one undo step, or one step per command?
   - How does the panel show what changed?
4. **Keys and privacy.**
   - Where do API keys live (the OS keychain)?
   - What is sent to a cloud model (the project data, the model geometry)?
   - How does an offline-only setting work (local models only)?
5. **Context size.** How does a large project (many operations, big meshes) fit a model's context window? Summaries, on-demand tool reads?
6. **Skills per tool.** One source of truth for the tool docs (generated from the MCP tool list?) with per-tool wrappers, so the docs never drift from the shipped tools.
7. **Tests.** Test the panel and the tool mapping without network access (a scripted fake provider).
8. **Clean room.** Only public API documentation of each provider and the MCP specification. No code or prompts copied from other CAM products.

Done means: one confine function called by both slot arms; a Trochoidal slot picked by two opposite edges is fitted or refused by name exactly like a Slot; the pins of #1504 and #1503 still pass.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

body:
Follow-up from #5 round 2 (staged on worktree agent-af493aee8d4f2d538, gated off).

The trochoid fallback (spiral -> trochoid -> rings) is wired in `pocket_hsm` / `pocket_troch` and plans the 22x60 channel end to end. One law keeps it off:

1. **Landing law (one descent per level).** Each microlift return ramps down onto the next front arc's start. That start is already in cut: the crescent ahead and the 0.33 mm wall strip are both inside the measuring rim (r + 1.5 cells). So `quality` counts a descent into stock every loop (118 for 2 levels against the law's 2). The spiral's lifted pieces avoid this with air leads. Trochoid arcs have no air lead that crosses no floor feed: a floor lead from inside the cleared area to the next start crosses the previous arc. Options to try: arcs whose ends sweep the wall strip clean (rho * sin(h) = half-width) plus a start ramp along the arc's own circle extension (crossing-free up to 90 deg + asin(s / 2 rho)), or non-circular loops whose start lies behind the previous envelope. Pinned by `troch_tests::a_landing_on_a_loop_start_in_cut_is_refused_by_name`. Remove the law's refusal once it holds.
2. **A practical step for thin bands (#13's 14 mm band).** It reads rho 1.90, s 0.103 and 2575 loops a level at the load. That is over the `LOOP_CAP` (600) and, before that, has no room to open out behind a helix. A closed band's trochoid is also not wired yet. It stays on the named Offset-rings fallback.
3. The 3-D ladder (`machining3d::hsm`) does not try the trochoid yet (`adaptive_passes(.., false)`).
